summary: Douglas County, OR lookout built 1933 on the Umpqua NF, gone by 1958; sources disagree on design (L-4 tower vs L-5 cab); no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 10 x 10 ft L-5 style cab on a 20-foot round timber tower (FFLOS and firelookout.com call it a 20-foot pole L-4 tower)
facts.status_note: Gone by 1958 per FFLOS and firelookout.com; Oregon lookouts page lists it as removed with no date. A 1953 survey station description refers to remains of a lookout tower 43 feet away.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com describe a 20-foot pole L-4 tower; Oregon lookouts and the FFLA describe an L-5 style 10 by 10 foot cab. The brief's L-5 is supported by two sources; the story reports both descriptions and does not pick one.
All four sources give a 20-foot tower, which matches the brief's 6.1 m.

sources.title: #firelookoutfriday post on the Clayton Point lookout
sources.publisher: Forest Fire Lookout Association on Instagram

notes_for_editor: Four sources, all agreeing on 1933 build and gone by 1958, but thin: no staffing, fire, or access information in any source read. FFLOS and firelookout.com probably share a data origin, so they are not independent. The FFLA post describes the area as southeastern Oregon while the other sources place the site in Douglas County; the story follows Douglas County. The 1953 survey station description is quoted second-hand from the Oregon lookouts page; the NGS datasheet itself was not fetched. Access is omitted because no source gives a level. Today's condition is unknown: no source describes the site now.
